notes.title: Garage update anouncement
notes.content:
🛠️ Devlog #34 – New Day, New Power-ups! 🌅
Hello dear friends,

Over the past month, we’ve been working hard on a big update featuring a fresh new gameplay mechanic!

As many of you know, our game leans into the rogue-lite genre. In this update, we’re introducing a clock and calendar system. Now, each time your character dies, you’ll wake up to a brand new day—but this time, you'll keep the money you earned! 💰

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/06199d4e7a8d65f82cf6d91c99dc2f4804d51473.png[/img]

With that, you’ll be able to purchase new furniture, power-ups, and other upgrades to make your next run even more exciting and personalized. Think of it as waking up stronger and more prepared—ready to face the challenges of a new day!

And yes... 🏡 we’ve added a garage! More on what you can do with it soon. 😉

🎨 Art Update
Our marketing illustrator has also been busy creating a brand new capsule collection for our Steam library. These new visuals are super vibrant and reflect the charm and quirky energy of the game. We can’t wait for you to see them live!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/879f7cd0d818fc02b2149203d9c1d71d87c85ff2.png[/img]

Thanks for sticking with us—your support keeps the game growing!
More updates coming very soon. Until then, stay rogue-y! ⚔️

— The Dev Team

notes.title: Interview with Our Sound Designer: Aleksandr Gurjev
notes.content:
🎧 Interview with Our Sound Designer: Aleksandr Gurjev
Behind the Sounds of “Adventures of Deliveryman”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/1fdee6c796398f2d66a6e770828f59a411557f2b.gif[/img]


We recently sat down with Aleksandr Gurjev, the composer and sound designer behind Adventures of Deliveryman, to learn more about the creative process behind the game’s unique and eclectic soundscape. From park raves to cinematic chases, Aleksandr shared his inspirations, challenges, and favorite sonic moments from the project.

1. What drew you to Adventures of Deliveryman? What clicked for you creatively?
Hi! My name is Aleksandr Gurjev, and I’m responsible for composing and sound designing for Adventures of Deliveryman. What immediately clicked for me was the opportunity to create an evolving musical world through a collection of in-game EPs. My vision was to build a library of tracks across multiple genres, bundle them into thematic 4-track EPs, and scatter them throughout the City as collectibles.
In the game’s lore, subliminal messaging has overtaken all media, and music as we know it has gone extinct. I wanted these lost records to act as fragments of the past — telling stories of a world before the silence, while also enhancing the player’s journey with atmospheric, expressive sounds.

2. How would you describe the sound identity of the game in one sentence?
A sweet and sour dish seasoned with chillies and drizzled with zest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/6cc688194946bafe1713b3dcd8ef81bd3c49d181.gif[/img]


3. Were there any specific locations or emotions in the game that inspired unique audio choices?
Absolutely. While living in Germany, I got to experience parts of the underground park rave scene, and that vibe really inspired how I approached some of the free-roam areas.
For mission stages, I leaned into a more cinematic, high-energy direction — reminiscent of chase scenes in action films. And during free ride moments, I pulled the tempo down to create a more relaxed, immersive feel, encouraging players to simply enjoy cruising through the City.

4. How did you build atmosphere through sound — especially in a game about delivery and exploration?
The concept of chase music was a huge anchor for me. I brought in orchestral elements, layered them with dynamic percussion, and played with momentum to mirror the fast-paced, goal-driven gameplay. Whether you're racing a timer or soaking in the cityscape, I wanted the soundtrack to reflect that energy and contrast.

5. What’s one sound in the game you’re especially proud of — and how did you create it?
Right now, I’m especially proud of the NPC hit sound pool. It took a while to nail — finding that sweet spot where the sound is dynamic, not annoying when repeated, and doesn’t punish players who play with higher volume settings. It’s punchy, playful, and has just the right amount of audio “squish.”

6. In a game focused on movement and momentum, how important is audio feedback for the player?
It’s absolutely critical. The sound needs to be snappy, short, and punchy, with a hint of arcade-style flavor. Timely audio feedback gives players a better sense of rhythm and responsiveness, and it adds to the game's flow — especially during high-speed sequences.

7. Did the narrative or characters influence your approach to sound design?
Definitely — one standout was the "bus chase" mission, where I composed with a more narrative-driven mindset, tying the tension of the moment into the music.
More broadly, all missions are time-oriented, so I used that pressure to inform musical pacing and intensity, reinforcing the stakes of each delivery.

8. Were there any creative challenges you had to overcome with a limited indie budget or time?
Oh, for sure — but I actually believe limitations spark creativity. I’ve found some clever ways to work within our current resources. That said, if the budget expands in the future, I already have ideas on where to invest — especially in refining dynamic systems and expanding our sound library.

9. What’s something players might not consciously notice, but you spent a lot of care on?
The number of fictional artists and alter egos that contributed to the in-game soundtrack. Each EP is designed to feel like it was made by a completely different artist, with its own identity and mood. My goal is for players to feel like they’re uncovering a lost musical culture — not just listening to tracks made by one person behind the curtain.

🎶 That’s a wrap for now — huge thanks to Aleksandr for taking us into the sonic layers of Adventures of Deliveryman. Stay tuned for more behind-the-scenes features!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/4d0e0d380294578395ad98ad1aeae33881a00e48.png[/img]

notes.title: Major Update for a full game
notes.content:
The time has finally come for a major game update. We've made the game's design more cohesive by introducing randomly assigned missions. However, it's not entirely random—your luck influences which missions drop from the pool. Completing all 32 missions marks the end of your workday as a delivery rider.

[previewyoutube=l6U_zjy_jLs;full][/previewyoutube]

Pedestrians now walk across fully rebuilt sidewalks made from 3D models. This should eliminate the bug where characters appeared to slide in place. We’ve also updated the controllers for all characters, ensuring smooth animation transitions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/6cc688194946bafe1713b3dcd8ef81bd3c49d181.gif[/img]

When approaching pedestrians, you will now see an emotion icon above their heads, indicating their current mood. There are three different states, each defining how the characters behave in the game. For example, some pedestrians turn aggressive and attack you if you nearly hit them with your bike. You can recognize them by the red angry icon above their heads. If you knock a pedestrian down, they will respawn as aggressive.

It’s important to note that emotion icons will only appear within the player's visible area on the screen. Our revamped NPCs interact with their surroundings in ways that make the city feel more real. Whether they’re reacting to your presence or simply living their own lives, these characters add a touch of humor and charm to your daily delivery adventures.

We've also added many new environmental elements to balance trick mechanics. Now that some railings in the city are slightly lower, you can grind on them like rails, using pedestrians' heads for momentum and performing Bunny Hop effects.

This is our first independently developed and released game, and the three of us continue working on improving the gameplay every week. Right now, we're preparing a major update, after which we’ve decided to finally release a demo version so players can experience the gameplay for free. Unfortunately, we have never released a demo version before.

notes.title: Struggling with soundtrack release ^_^
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/1fdee6c796398f2d66a6e770828f59a411557f2b.gif[/img]

Today, we fixed the timeline for all tracks for the Steam upload. It was necessary to match the track names with the timeline in the CSV file. The thing is, if your tracks aren’t numbered, the system won’t link them correctly with the names in the table.

We finally submitted the corrected Adventures of Deliveryman soundtrack build for Steam review. Hopefully, as planned, we’ll release our soundtrack on February 21.

We're working on a major update where our characters will actually walk on the ground instead of sliding like before. We’ve completely reworked the state machine for characters.

There are also a lot of invisible actions in our game. For example, pedestrians have different states that trigger behavior—some get angry and start running at you. To help players recognize pedestrians' emotions, we gave them different icons that appear above their heads.

notes.title: Our Game Soundtrack Is Finally on Steam! 🎶
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/6504e5dd4ae29b67c83d4b02e5797e9063f40e3a.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]We spent the whole day battling interfaces just to finally upload our game’s soundtrack to Steam.[/b][/h1]

So it will be released 21 FEB 2024

This soundtrack was created for us by Alexander Guryev over the three years of development. You’ll hear a fusion of old-school urban electronics mixed with unrestrained fun in it. Every track carries a hint of the early 2000s - a time when electronic music was revolutionizing traditional instruments.

Our inspiration comes from the minimalist spirit of suprematism, set against the backdrop of an average Eastern European city. Some of Alexander’s tracks were written under different pseudonyms, creating the illusion of a simulated radio station playing through a portable music player.

Your feedback and ideas are critical to us, as this is our first game. Please don’t hesitate to leave a review if you purchase the soundtrack!

notes.title: Our physics system now works much better than before!
notes.content:
This week I have also prepared a new game description - check this out:

A simple and incredibly charming game about a bike courier, where you can have fun exploring the city on a bicycle and playing with physics. Ride around, knock over pedestrians in your path, grind rails in spectacular slides during your deliveries, or pull off aerial stunts. But the coolest part? You can become a true extreme master, defying the laws of physics and space! Imagine: you do a backflip off a rooftop, land in a slide, and top it all off with a combo that doubles your points!

The action takes place in an open city full of life: crowds of people are rushing about their business, heading from home to work or to the store. Thousands of pedestrians will block your way, making it harder to deliver packages on time. And if the pedestrians aren't enough of an obstacle, beware of villains behind the wheel of cars—they’ll try to knock you down on your route.

All tricks can be chained into combos, bringing bonus points. Complete missions, collect upgrade cards, and level up your bike. Upgrades can be installed directly in the garage through a handy menu.

But be careful: death in the game is permanent. If you fail, you'll have to start over from the beginning. However, with each attempt, you'll gain new knowledge and experience, allowing you to progress faster and sharpen your skills to perfection.

The game spans one intense and action-packed day in the life of a delivery service courier. Are you ready for the challenge? 🚴‍♂️
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/7be489d4b67ea5feb77a7422340cbf0145c84fd5.png[/img]
Our physics system now works much better than before! You can use your bike to ride through cars, allowing you to pull off even cooler tricks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/59068ff7f9d560c11e2e5a9c15b5ecff60c366fa.png[/img]
Using trash bags, you can now fly much higher than buildings! This is a really cool feature—sometimes you can fly over 100 meters, making parcel delivery faster and more exciting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44637108/5688df3e325a8af3d54a9a69a0f59cf5b430bd96.png[/img]
We’ve also added a day and night cycle! At night, you can use your flashlight to see obstacles more clearly.

notes.title: Adventure of Deliveryman Needs Your Wheel
notes.content:
🌊 Expanded Environment: The city is now surrounded by a vast sea.
🎮 Improved Controls: Controls have been optimized for smoother riding using a gamepad or a mousepad with a keyboard.
[img]https://shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/1997940/extras/quest.gif?t=1732665345[/img]
📦 Revamped Missions: We now offer 23 unique delivery missions to complete.
🚗 Dynamic City Traffic: Moving cars have been added throughout the city—some are quite speedy!
🤸 Double Jump and Rail Slides: Perform double jumps to land on rails and slide for faster movement.
🚴‍♂️ Bicycle Customization: Unlock parts through game progression! Collect cards (tokens) to upgrade bicycle parts and enhance stats.
🎯 Combo Mechanics: Keep track of your combo moves with a score counter to see how much you’ve earned.
🌬 Air Physics Tweaks: Enjoy more realistic aerial movement.
💨 Drift Physics: Experience smoother and more enjoyable bicycle drifting.
🗺 Quest Path Generator: Navigate through nonlinear game progression with ease.

We hope you enjoy all the new features and enhancements. 🚵‍♀️ Happy riding! 🚴‍♀️
